title: KPI hypothesis lab — sprint scratchpad
content:
KPI hypothesis lab — sprint scratchpad
Owner: Aisha Rao (personal tracking)
Context: quick, messy place to iterate on objective + KRs for inference cost/latency work I own. Not a polished PRD — use this to capture hypotheses, weekly observations, tiny experiments, and quick asks for SE/infra.

OBJECTIVE (draft): Reduce 95th-percentile inference latency and cost for short chat use-cases while keeping >= 98% quality parity with baseline model v1.2.

Key results (initial proposals):
KR1: Reduce hosted API p95 latency for chat (<= 128 tokens) from 220ms -> 150ms (region: us-west)
KR2: Lower cost-per-1M-tokens served on common T4/Dedicated path by 20% vs current baseline (baseline = $12.8 per 1M tokens)
KR3: Keep end-user instruction-following eval pass rate >= 98% on 10 curated prompt set (ref: eval-set-001)

BASELINES (measured 2025-10-20):
- p95 latency (us-west, chat, <=128 tokens): 220ms
- cost per 1M tokens (avg across small batches): $12.8
- eval pass rate (eval-set-001): 98.9%
- avg batch size observed (hosted): 2.1

HYPOTHESIS + EXPERIMENTS (working log)
H1: Small-batch adaptive batching will reduce p95 without increasing mean latency.
- experiment: enable continuous batching window = 10ms, max batch size = 8 on experiment route (route: chat/fast/h1).
- metric targets: p95 drop >= 20ms, mean change <= +5ms.
- result (2025-11-10): p95 -18ms, mean +3ms. Slightly short of target but promising.
- next: try dynamic window (10ms -> 5ms during low QPS) and measure p95 across traffic curve.

H2: KV-cache prefix promotion for short prompts cuts token compute by 12-18% without quality regression.
- experiment: enable prefix promotion on dedicated pool with cached prefixes for top-100 prompts.
- result (2025-11-17): compute tokens saved = 14%, eval pass rate = 98.7% (within noise).
- next: widen to top-500, add eviction policy, monitor cold-hit tail.

H3: Quantization profile Q4 (8-bit mixed) lowers cost but may affect rare instruction-following cases.
- experiment: deploy q8-mixed on canary 5% traffic for non-sensitive tenants.
- result (2025-11-24): cost delta -12%, eval pass rate down by 0.8pp on edge-case suite.
- decision: hold for now; design fallback for instruction-heavy requests.

WEEKLY CHECK-INS (personal quick notes)
- 2025-11-10:
  * Focus: batching window tuning + baseline run. Saw stable cpu/gpu utilization.
  * Blocker: observability trace for micro-batching dropped traces during overflow. Filed JIRA JIRA-ENG-1423.
  * Action: ask infra for span retention bump for 48h.

- 2025-11-17:
  * Focus: cache hit analysis, ran synthetic workload to measure cold-start tail.
  * Insight: 60% of requests share top-200 prefixes (higher than expected). Good signal for prefix cache ROI.
  * TODO: synthesize list of top-500 prefixes and push to repo/ops as artifact.

- 2025-11-24:
  * Focus: q8-mixed canary, collected quality diffs.
  * Finding: q8 impacts hallucination rate on instruction window > 512 tokens (rare for chat short-case).
  * Action: add per-route quantization policy to avoid q8 for >=512 token requests.

RETRO (quick)
- What worked:
  * Small-batch tuning gave low-friction wins without infra changes.
  * Observability improvements let me link p95 spikes to GC events vs queueing latency.
- What didn't:
  * Canary rollout process had friction — infra ops manual gate slowed experiment iteration. Need self-service canaries.
  * Some eval-edge cases were not covered by eval-set-001 -> added two new categories (context-switching, long-instruction chains).

DECISIONS TO PROPOSE (for 1:1 / team review)
1) Move forward with adaptive batching as a configurable route-level policy (owner: me).
2) Approve prefix-caching expansion to top-500 prefixes and instrument cold-hit alarms (owner: infra + me).
3) Do not roll q8-mixed globally; create per-route opt-in with automatic rollback on eval regressions.

OPEN QUESTIONS / NOTES TO MANAGER
- Can we get a small budget to run heavy synthetic workloads on Dedicated for 48h? (Estimate: 2x p4d-slices, cost approx $3k)
- Who owns the canary gate automation? Need quick path to 10% -> 50% without SRE oncall.
- Should I prioritize reducing p95 vs cost? I think p95 first (user-visible), then cost via q-profiles.

NEXT ACTIONS (short list)
- Draft short RFC for adaptive batching policy (due 2025-12-01).
- Prepare top-500 prefix artifact and open infra PR to seed caches (by 2025-12-05).
- Prototype canary automation script (python + GH action) and demo in weekly sync (2025-12-08).
- Book 1:1 with Diego next week to align on the infra budget ask.

SCRATCH / RANDOM NOTES
- Quick metric snippet to paste in slack: "hosted-chat p95 us-west: 220ms -> 202ms w/ H1 (10ms window); expecting 150ms after dynamic window tuning"
- Eval link: confluence/eng/evals/eval-set-001 (add new categories: context-switch, long-instr)
- Related tickets: JIRA-ENG-1423 (observability), JIRA-ENG-1499 (canary automation), JIRA-ENG-1510 (prefix seeding)

Very rough; will clean after decision cycle. Notes to self: keep experiments small, prefer route-level config changes, and record exact perf runs (timestamp + commit) for reproducibility.

---
End of scratchpad.
